figures.caption: Figure 1: Dual-view EEG learning. A fixed PSD–logistic-regression sensor expert maps scalp spectra to a diagnostic probability, and a source expert anchors sLORETA activity to a healthy-dynamics prior (pretrained on healthy EEG only) and deforms it with a low-rank sparse solver into an explicit ROI×frequency×lag state. The two experts combine only at a fixed decision level, leaving the two branches architecturally separate and the source state available for attribution.

Table 2: Strict subject-level holdout comparison under a unified local reproduction protocol (three seeds; mean±std). All learning-based baselines were reproduced under the same subject-level evaluation protocol. Scalp PSD + LR is also used as the fixed Sensor Expert in DMD-EEG; DMD-EEG-Source is the source-space neural-dynamics deformation branch; DMD-EEG (Full) combines the two experts with fixed equal-weight decision fusion (α=0.5). AUPRC and F1pos use disease as the positive class. Within each task and metric, bold marks the best result and underline the second best.

Table 3: Complementarity of sensor and source views in DMD-EEG. The Sensor Expert is a fixed Scalp PSD + logistic-regression classifier; the Source Expert predicts directly from the deformation state ∆h (DMD-EEG-Source), with solver depth selected per dataset (K=4, r=1 for MDD; K=3, r=1 for FEP; K=2, r=2 for PD). DMD-EEG (Full) fuses the two experts with fixed equal weights (α=0.5). Sensor–Source Corr. is the Spearman correlation between the pooled out-of-sample predictions of the two experts; F1pos is the positive-class F1. Within each disease and metric, bold marks the best branch and underline the second best.

Table 5: Complete fixed 46-ROI atlas. L and R are distinct source coordinates. The names are the analysis labels used throughout the code and result records. Design groups record the inclusion rationale fixed before disease-model evaluation.

Table 7: Solver depth and rank scan on the real-lag scale-axis (per-τ ACF) under the strict three-seed protocol (mean±std over seeds), including the one-shot (K=1) and no-deformation (K=0) controls. Candidates are the K≥2 rows; the bold row is the inner-validation argmax over its disease’s candidates. The control rows (K=1 and K=0) fall outside the candidate set. ∗The no-deformation (K=0) row bypasses the solver entirely and routes the anchor state h0 directly to the linear head, so it isolates the contribution of the iterative deformation beyond a zero-input control. The holdout columns are a post-selection check.

Table 8: Healthy-dynamics pretraining ablation under the strict three-seed protocol (mean±std over seeds). “Full” is the reported configuration with the disease’s selected solver depth and rank (Table 7); “scratch” trains the same configuration from an empty pretrained checkpoint, so the healthy-dynamics prior is removed. The K=1 and K=0 deformation controls are in Table 7.

Table 9: Paired ∆AUC of the α=0.5 fusion against each single branch. Fold-level rows report mean±std over the three holdout folds (folds with positive ∆AUC in parentheses). Subject-level rows report a paired bootstrap over the pooled holdout subjects (n=33/48/90; 20000 resamples; 95% percentile CI). Bold marks the comparison whose 95% CI excludes zero.

Table 10: Fixed subject-level five-fold reference, mean±std. Not the primary estimate. Ensemble rows (†) are persubject logit averages of the two readouts. The strict-holdout results in the main text use the direct deformation readout. This 5-fold table additionally includes the communication-pathway readout as a development comparison. The no-deformation (K=0) control is reported in Table 7.

Table 13: Source-level lag perturbation at the solver input (three-seed mean ∆AUC relative to the identity perturbation; chosen-fold checkpoint on fold-validation subjects). The incremental rows add lag on top of band or ROI, with the increment over the single-axis perturbation in parentheses.

Table 14: Attribution readout of the healthy-anchored state hhealth. ROI importance is the unsigned amplitude saliency meansubj|∂ logit/∂hhealth| (consensus over 3 splits× 3 folds), cross-seed stable (axis cosine 0.83–0.87) and concordant with the occlusion test below (ROI Spearman +0.31 MDD, +0.59 PD). The spectro-temporal signature is the ROI-marginal signed saliency profile, carrying band and lag direction and selectivity. Each coordinate sits on a real axis: ROI and band inherited from the input, lag the real per-τ autocorrelation (τ ∈ {1, 2, 4, 8}). A band/lag (+) sign means the patient-versus-healthy logit rises as that coordinate increases, marking a direction of decision sensitivity, distinct from a change in brain activity. Directional saliency findings.

Table 15: ROI occlusion on the healthy-anchored state. AUC drop (mean±std over the three seed checkpoints, chosen fold) when the occluded set’s band × lag block is zeroed and the holdout is re-scored. Single ROIs are ranked by occlusion magnitude over all 46 ROIs; joint sets (†) are occlusion-search results and exploratory. The permutation p over random same-size block sets (internal null, n=300) is nominal and uncorrected for the search over 46 ROIs, so the table is a descriptive ranking only.

Figure 2: Decision-sensitivity attribution maps of the healthy-anchored state (same 46 ROI× 5 band× 4 lag grid as Figure 3). Color is the 3-seed consensus unsigned sensitivity meansubj|∂ logit/∂hhealth|, normalized so 1.0 is uniform (white = 0, deeper red = more sensitive); circles mark coordinates in the consensus top-10 and in≥ 2/3 seeds’ top-20. This map asks where the decision is sensitive, Figure 3 where the state differs; the two are complementary. ROI-level attribution is cross-seed stable (axis cosine 0.83–0.87), cell-level values only weakly stable, and sensitivity differs from decision-dependence (Table 15).

Figure 3: Source-state effect maps of the final deformed state hK (46 ROI × 5 bands × 4 lags), same 3-seed fullcohort protocol as Figure 2. Rows are the 46 ROIs grouped by atlas origin (MDD-core 22 / FEP-ext 12 / PD-ext 8 / robust 4; white lines separate groups); columns are the five bands, each split into lags {1, 2, 4, 8}. Color is the mean Cohen’s d (patient− HC) of the per-subject final state on a fixed±1.0 axis (red = patients more positive, blue = more negative). Circles mark coordinates whose d sign is consistent across seeds and whose |d| is in the top-k. Descriptive effect maps, distinct from significance maps.

Figure 4: Per-subject deformation trajectory and state geometry (descriptive; one representative checkpoint per panel, cv-pool subjects seen in training). Left: the disease-axis projection ⟨∆hk, ŵ⟩ as the solver iterates k (thin lines, subjects; solid line, group mean ± std); monotone group separation indicates the deviation emerges during solving. Right: the two directions of largest cross-subject variance of hhealth (920-dim) define a shared 2D plane with per-subject points (HC blue, patients red), group-mean squares, one HC→patient offset arrow (direction real; length scaled for visibility, offset in σ annotated), and per-subject quiver arrows of the decision gradient ∂ logit/∂hhealth (direction = where the state must move to raise the patient probability; length = sensitivity). Axes are normalized per principal direction to σ units on a fixed ±3.5σ range shared across diseases.

Figure 5: Receiver operating characteristic of the Sensor Expert, Source Expert, and DMD-EEG (Full) on the pooled subjects of the three non-overlapping holdouts (each subject predicted once; n=33 MDD, 48 FEP, 90 PD). Fusion in dark blue, Sensor in amber, Source in sage green; open circles mark the fixed 0.5-threshold operating point that determines BAcc/F1. AUC here is the pooled value over concatenated holdout subjects and differs from the per-seed mean±std in Tables 3 and 2. Fusion is competitive with and complementary to the best single branch: on MDD a positive trend over both branches, on FEP matching the strong source branch, on PD exceeding the source branch while matching the sensor. Fusion and sensor can share the 0.5-threshold point, hence the same BAcc, while differing in AUC; the ROC separates ranking quality from the operating point. Curves are piecewise linear because the empirical ROC has finitely many thresholds.

Figure 6: Sensor versus Source predicted probabilities (P (patient); HC blue, patients red). Shapes encode which branch is correct: ◦ both, △ sensor only, ▽ source only, × both wrong (counts in legend). The 0.5 threshold lines define four quadrants; the two disagreement quadrants are shaded and the dashed y=x line marks agreement. Pooled Pearson correlations (on the panels): MDD r=0.55, FEP 0.26, PD 0.13. Points in the disagreement triangles are subjects one branch gets wrong and the other recovers; sensor-only/source-only counts are 4/3 (MDD), 7/10 (FEP), 18/15 (PD). On PD both branches err on many subjects and the source branch is weaker, so the fusion stays sensordominated.

Figure 7: Disease pathway glass brains (MNI ortho views). Two quantities are overlaid and should be kept distinct. Node selection and size encode decision sensitivity: the eight ROIs with the highest unsigned amplitude attribution |∂ logit/∂hhealth| (3-seed full-cohort, cross-seed stable). Node color encodes the case−HC state offset E[h | case] − E[h | HC] (red = higher in patients, blue = lower), per disease normalized; a group-level representational difference, separate from a decision quantity. The two can differ. Arrows are an illustrative minimum-spanningtree pathway directed from smaller to larger offset, independent of learned connectivity. Circuit labels: MDD frontolimbic-temporal, FEP fronto-parietal (insular), PD sensorimotor (insular). Colors and sizes are per-disease normalized, so absolute magnitudes are comparable only within a disease; offsets are group-level and correlational, without a causal claim, and deep ROIs (amygdala, hippocampus) are sLORETA source estimates.
